'''Stefan Bernhard''' (born 1966) is a Swiss scientist who has worked in fields related to the interaction between light and [[transition metal complex]]es. His involvement in the prediction, generation, and spectroscopy of [[Circular polarization|circularly polarized]] luminescence from synthesized [[Chirality (chemistry)|chiral]] [[phosphors]] have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art in this relatively young sub-field of photophysical chemistry.<ref>{{cite journal
| title      = Synthesis, Separation, and Circularly Polarized Luminescence Studies of Enantiomers of Iridium(III) Luminophores
| journal       =  Inorganic Chemistry
|volume = 47| issue       = 6
| pages       = 2039–2048
| last1       = Oyler
| first1      = Karl
| last2      = Coughlin
| first2     = Frederick
| last3      = Bernhard
| first3     = Stefan
| last4      = Westrol
| first4     = Michael
| date       = 2008-02-14
| doi      = 10.1021/ic701747j
| pmid       = 18271527
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| title      = Controlling the Helicity of 2,2'-Bipyridyl Ruthenium(II) and Zinc(II) Hemicage Complexes
| journal       =  Journal of the American Chemical Society
|volume = 129| issue       = 1
| pages       = 210–217
| last1       = Oyler
| first1      = Karl
| last2      = Coughlin
| first2     = Frederick
| last3      = Bernhard
| first3     = Stefan
| date       = 2006-12-09
| doi      = 10.1021/ja067016v
| pmid       = 17199301
}}</ref>  Other contributions involve work in [[artificial photosynthesis]] and [[organic light-emitting diode]]s.

==Contributions==
'''Circularly Polarized Luminescence Spectroscopy (CPL)'''<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Riehl |first1=James P. |last2=Richardson |first2=Frederick S. |date=1986-02-01 |title=Circularly polarized luminescence spectroscopy |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cr00071a001 |journal=Chemical Reviews |volume=86 |issue=1 |pages=1–16 |doi=10.1021/cr00071a001 |issn=0009-2665|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Capable of measuring dissymmetry factors of even weakly luminescent materials to within a reported error as small as 10<sup>−6</sup>,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Oyler |first1=Karl D. |last2=Coughlin |first2=Frederick J. |last3=Bernhard |first3=Stefan |date=2007-01-01 |title=Controlling the Helicity of 2,2'-Bipyridyl Ruthenium(II) and Zinc(II) Hemicage Complexes |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja067016v |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=129 |issue=1 |pages=210–217 |doi=10.1021/ja067016v |pmid=17199301 |bibcode=2007JAChS.129..210O |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> the home-built CPL spectrometer created and used by the Bernhard lab is more sensitive than any previously demonstrated CPL spectrometer. In addition, it was shown that CPL dissymmetry factors can be predicted computationally<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Coughlin |first1=Frederick J. |last2=Westrol |first2=Michael S. |last3=Oyler |first3=Karl D. |last4=Byrne |first4=Neal |last5=Kraml |first5=Christina |last6=Zysman-Colman |first6=Eli |last7=Lowry |first7=Michael S. |last8=Bernhard |first8=Stefan |date=2008-03-01 |title=Synthesis, Separation, and Circularly Polarized Luminescence Studies of Enantiomers of Iridium(III) Luminophores |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ic701747j |journal=Inorganic Chemistry |volume=47 |issue=6 |pages=2039–2048 |doi=10.1021/ic701747j |pmid=18271527 |issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription }}</ref> over a diverse sampling of known luminophore architectures, validating a new and facile tool for directing synthetic efforts in the search for anisotropic emitters.

Efforts in this field have focused on solution-based water photolysis. '''Organic light emitting devices'''

The primary outcome of work in this field has been ionic transition metal complex devices with improved turn-on times, achieved by A) [http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cm050314r employing ionic liquids], or B) [http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=20000207 attaching cationic tails of varying lengths to the luminophores].

==Education==

* '''Lab Technician Apprenticeship''' ''(1982-1985)'' at [http://everything2.com/title/Tobler Suchard Tobler Chocolates]
* '''Diploma in Chemical Engineering''' ''(1985-1988)'' from the School of Engineering in [[Burgdorf, Switzerland]]
* '''Diploma in Chemistry''' ''(1988-1993)'' from the [[University of Fribourg]], Switzerland
* '''Doctorate of Philosophy in Chemistry''' ''(1993-1996)'' from the [[University of Fribourg]] for "synthesis and properties of [[adamantane]] bridged diimine ligands and their Ru(II) and Os(II) complexes" under Prof. Dr. [http://www.chem.unifr.ch/pb/ Peter Belser]
* '''Postdoctoral Research Associate''' ''(1996-1998)'' at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] under Dr. Jon Schoonover.  Supported by fellowships from the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] and the Novartis Foundation
* '''Postdoctoral Research Associate''' ''(1998-2002)'' at [[Cornell University]] under Prof. Dr. [[Héctor D. Abruña]].  Supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation Fellowship for Advanced Researchers

==Career==

* '''Assistant Professorship''' ''(2002-2009)'' in the Department of Chemistry at [[Princeton University]].  During this assignment, Prof. Dr. Bernhard was awarded A) the Dreyfus New Faculty award, B) the NSF Career award, and C) Princeton's graduate mentoring award, as well as endorsement for promotion from Princeton's existing chemistry faculty.
* '''Associate Professorship''' ''(2009-present)'' in the Department of Chemistry at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].<ref>{{cite web
| url        = http://www.chem.cmu.edu/groups/bernlab/
| title      = Bernlab: Chemistry With a Twist
| accessdate = 2014-08-16
}}</ref>
